ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r4.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.claim: Prosperity tests gratitude and care for others rather than pride and usurpation; hardship tests contentment rather than despair, and people should examine their treatment of orphans and the poor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r3.anchor: with the orphans and the poor after receiving

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r1.claim: Affluent leaders of Makkah and Ṭā’if are reproached: wealth is a test calling for gratitude and service to orphans and the poor, but instead made them proud and contemptuous.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r1.anchor: the affluent leaders of Makkah and Ṭā’if are addressed directly and admonished.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r3.claim: The verb for urging means exhorting one another; society should actively encourage orphan welfare rather than conceal stinginess, and “food” broadly means meeting all their needs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p311/r3.anchor: The objective is to cater for all their needs.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p474/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p474/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p474/r9.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Shayba, the Kufans, and Ibn Muqsim read taḥāḍḍūn with an open tāʾ and alif, from tataḥāḍḍūn: urging one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p474/r9.anchor: وأبو جعفر وشيبة والكوفيون وابن مقسم: تحاضون بفتح التاء والألف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p474/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p474/r10.speaker: عبد الله وعلقمة وزيد بن علي وابن المبارك والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p474/r10.claim: These authorities read the same form with a damma on tāʾ, “you urge yourselves”; reciprocal and mutual verb forms can also mean a simple verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p474/r10.anchor: وعبد الله أو علقمة وزيد بن علي وعبد الله بن المبارك والشيرزي

NAHHAS:v5p223/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p223/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p223/r1.claim: The object is omitted because listeners know it: people are not urging others to feed the poor.
NAHHAS:v5p223/r1.anchor: حذف المفعول لعلم السامع أي ولا تحضون الناس

NAHHAS:v5p223/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p223/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p223/r2.claim: The reading taḥāḍḍūn is understood as tataḥāḍḍūn with one tāʾ deleted, as in 3:103.
NAHHAS:v5p223/r2.anchor: قدره بمعنى تتحاضون حذفت إحدى التائين

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r7.claim: The rebuke means they neither encourage one another nor command charity to feed the poor; wealth was given for this care.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r7.anchor: أي ولا تحثون على إطعامه ولا تأمرون بالتصدق عليه

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r8.claim: The reading la tahadduna means that people do not urge one another to feed the poor.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ لا تحاضون أراد لا يحض بعضكم بعضا على ذلك

TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r9.claim: The passage locates humiliation in neglecting orphans and withholding charity, not in poverty itself.
TABRISI:89:1-30#8/r9.anchor: والمعنى أن الإهانة ما فعلتموه من ترك إكرام اليتيم ومنع الصدقة من الفقير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:18-25/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:18-25/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:18-25/r1.claim: They neither urge one another to feed the poor nor help with it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:18-25/r1.anchor: { ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين } لا تأمرون به، ولا تعينون عليه.

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r7.claim: People should compete in urging one another to feed and care for the poor, but instead they discourage it and may seek to exploit them.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r7.anchor: birbirinizle müsabaka etmeniz lâzım gelirken siz bilakis ondan kaçınıyor, birbirinizi tenfir ediyorsunuz

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r8.claim: The reciprocal verb is originally tatāhāddūn; Nafi, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn Amir read it with a damma on ha and without the alif.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r8.anchor: Nâfi‘, İbn Kesîr, İbn Âmir kıraatlerinde hâ’nın zammıyla elifsiz

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read the verbs throughout in the third-person plural: they honor, urge, consume, and love.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r9.anchor: Ebû Amr ve Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde de bu fiiller hep yâ ile gāib sîgası üzerine

ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.claim: These failures come from neglecting the afterlife and God’s watch; people should use their present opportunity for good, honor orphans, feed the poor, and prepare for the hereafter.
ELMALILI:89:16-26#2/r14.anchor: Bütün bunlar âhireti düşünmemek, Hak teâlâ’nın mirsâd ile gözetmekte olduğunu hesâba almamaktan neş’et eder

BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r1.claim: Using an orphan's labor without wages is forbidden even for a brother or teacher, except in the cited case of a mother or sending the child to fetch his partner, according to al-Ashbah and al-Qunya.
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r1.anchor: استخدام اليتيم بلا أجرة حرام ولو لأخيه ومعلمه إلا لأمه

BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r2.claim: The verse means people neither feed the poor nor encourage one another to do so; deleting a repeated tāʾ is a grammatical shortening, and failing to urge others makes their own failure to feed even more blameworthy.
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r2.anchor: والحض الحث والتحريض لا يحض بعضكم بعضا ولا يحث من أهل وغيره

BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r3.speaker: مقاتل
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r3.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed because Qudama ibn Maz'un, an orphan in Umayya ibn Khalaf's care, was denied his rights.
BURSEVI:v10p331#3/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل كان قدامة بن مظعون يتيما في حجر أمية بن خلف

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#2/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#2/r2.claim: A report says Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf recited the clauses about honoring the orphan and urging food for the poor with the yā' form.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3428#2/r2.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرا بل لا يكرمون اليتيم ولا يحضون بالياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r1.claim: Bal shifts from the claim that wealth is honor to the contradiction: these people hoard their surplus instead of honoring God's needy servants, exposing their boast of generosity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r1.anchor: فنبههم الله على أنهم إن أكرمهم الله فإنهم لم يكرموا عبيده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r5.claim: Failure even to urge feeding the poor implies, all the more, failure to feed them; their indifference means they will not even advocate for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r5.anchor: دلالة فحوى الخطاب ، أي لقلة الاكتراث بالمساكين لا ينفعونهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r6.claim: Ṭaʿām may mean food, making the poor the beneficiaries, or be the verbal noun of feeding, making them its object and the rich those to be urged.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r6.anchor: يجوز أن يكون اسما بمعنى المطعوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r7.claim: Miskīn means a poor person, as discussed in Sūrat al-Tawbah.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p332/r8.claim: The verse uses ellipsis to imply that they neither urge orphan guardians to honor their wards nor feed the poor from their own wealth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r1.claim: Urging others to feed the poor can stand for feeding them oneself, since someone who advocates an act is willing to do it when able; the same usage occurs in the command to counsel truth and patience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r1.anchor: من يحض على فعل شيء يكون راغبا في التلبس به فإذا تمكن أن يفعله فعله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.claim: The majority use second-person verbs to turn from speaking about the human to confronting the offenders; Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb use third person to expose them to the Prophet and believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : ( لا تكرمون ، ولا تحضون ، وتأكلون ، وتحبون ) بالمثناة الفوقية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r3.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r3.claim: These readers use taḥāḍḍūn with an open ḥāʾ and an alif, a reciprocal verb whose underlying form drops one of two adjacent tāʾs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r3.anchor: وقرأه عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف { تحاضون } بفتح الحاء وألف بعدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r4.claim: On the reciprocal reading, they mutually encourage one another to refrain from urging others to feed the poor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p333/r4.anchor: أي تتمالؤون على ترك الحض على الإطعام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r10.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r10.claim: They read yahuddun, meaning people encourage one another or encourage themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p479#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر «يحضون» بمعنى: يحض بعضهم بعضا أو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r1.claim: The preceding reading's continuation allows self-encouragement; the following variant is reciprocal encouragement.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r2.claim: Their tahāḍḍūn reading means that people urge one another to feed the needy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي «تحاضون» بفتح التاء بمعنى تتحاضون، أي يحض قوم قوما،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r3.claim: Abu Amr reads yahuddun with a yāʾ and without the alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r3.anchor: «يحضون» بياء من تحت مفتوحة وبغير ألف،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak reads with ḍamma on tāʾ, meaning that people urge themselves or one another; the source analyzes it as a reciprocal form used with a simpler sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن المبارك «تحاضون» بضم التاء على وزن تقاتلون، أي أنفسكم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r5.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r5.claim: Al-A'mash reads tatāḥāḍḍūn with two tāʾs.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r6.claim: Ṭaʿām here can mean feeding; alternatively it can mean the food itself with an omitted phrase about giving the needy person his food.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r6.anchor: وطعام في هذه الآية بمعنى إطعام، وقال قوم: أراد نفس طعامه الذي يأكل، ففي الكلام حذف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r7.claim: The passage previously treated the meanings of miskin and faqir in Surat al-Tawba, so he does not repeat that discussion here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p480/r7.anchor: وقد تقدم القول في (سورة براءة) في المسكين والفقير بمعنى يغني عن إعادته،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120#2/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and the Kufans read taḥāḍḍūn with an alif and fatḥa on tāʾ; al-Kisāʾī's transmission agrees except with ḍamma on tāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة تحاضون بألف مع فتح التاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120#2/r2.claim: They do not urge one another to feed the poor because they do not hope for the afterlife's reward; this supports the first interpretation of the previous verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p120#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى لا يأمرون بإطعامه لأنهم لا يرجون ثواب الآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p399/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p399/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p399/r1.claim: People neither encourage one another to feed the poor nor urge charity for needy people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p399/r1.anchor: يعني: لا يأمرون بالإحسان إلى الفقراء والمساكين، ويحث بعضهم على بعض في ذلك،

FARRA:v3p261/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r8.speaker: عاصم والأعمش
FARRA:v3p261/r8.claim: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read taḥāḍḍūna with alif and fatḥa on tāʾ.
FARRA:v3p261/r8.anchor: ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين (18) قرأ الأعمش وعاصم بالألف وفتح التاء،

FARRA:v3p261/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r9.speaker: أهل المدينة
FARRA:v3p261/r9.claim: Medinan readers use taḥuḍḍūna without the alif.
FARRA:v3p261/r9.anchor: (18) قرأ الأعمش وعاصم بالألف وفتح التاء، وقرأ أهل المدينة: «ولا تحضون»

FARRA:v3p261/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r10.speaker: الحسن البصري
FARRA:v3p261/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī reads yaḥuḍḍūna, “they urge one another,” and eats the orphan’s food in the adjacent clause.
FARRA:v3p261/r10.anchor: وفتح التاء، وقرأ أهل المدينة: «ولا تحضون» ، وقرأ الحسن البصري : «ويحضون، ويأكلون

FARRA:v3p261/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r11.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v3p261/r11.claim: Another reading raises the tāʾ in taḥāḍḍūna; all these readings are sound.
FARRA:v3p261/r11.anchor: الحسن البصري : «ويحضون، ويأكلون » ، وقد قرأ بعضهم: «تحاضون » برفع التاء، وكل صواب.

FARRA:v3p261/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p261/r12.claim: Taḥāḍḍūna can mean protecting/urging one another; taḥuḍḍūna means ordering people to feed the poor; the reciprocal form means urging each other.
FARRA:v3p261/r12.anchor:
صواب.
كأن «تحاضون» تحافظون، وكأن، «تحضون» تأمرون بإطعامه ، وكأن تحاضون: يحض بعضكم

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read the four verbs “honor,” “urge,” “eat,” and “love” in the third person; others address the listeners directly.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r11.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب الأربعة كلها بالياء

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r12.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read taḥāḍḍūn with alif as reciprocal urging—people urging one another.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r12.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: تحاضون بفتح التاء والألف

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r13.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r13.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read taḥuḍḍūn without an alif.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r13.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر: تحضون بالتاء وضم الحاء من غير ألف

JISHUMI:v10p7402/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r14.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r14.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb use the third-person yāʾ form without alif; al-Kisāʾī is also reported with a ḍamma on tāʾ and an alif.
JISHUMI:v10p7402/r14.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب بالياء وضم الحاء بغير ألف

JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.claim: The rebuke “rather, you do not honor” answers the claim that restricted provision means God is humiliating people: their own neglect is the fault.
JISHUMI:v10p7405/r2.anchor: لما رد عليهم ظنهم أن التقدير الإهانة، بين أن الإهانة لهذا، لا لما قالوا

JISHUMI:v10p7409/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r4.claim: The verse establishes an obligation to protect the rights of the poor.
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r4.anchor: ويدل على وجوب رعاية حق الفقراء

JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.claim: Eating, loving, honoring, and urging are human acts, as shown by the praise and blame attached to them.
JISHUMI:v10p7409/r6.anchor: ويدل أن هذا الأكل والحب والإكرام والحض فعل العبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r2.claim: The encouragement phrase has a variant with yā or tā; Ibn Masud reads the tā with ḍamma as mutual encouragement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p754/r2.anchor: وقرىء ( يكرمون ) وما بعده بالياء والتاء

MUQATIL:89:15-22/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r4.claim: After a break in the discourse, Muqātil resumes the criticism of Umayya: people fail to honor orphans or urge feeding the poor because they do not expect the Hereafter.
MUQATIL:89:15-22/r4.anchor: ثم انقطع الكلام، ثم ذكر أمية بن خلف الجمحي، وذكر مساوئه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p338/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338/r1.claim: A greater fault than their mistaken claim about wealth is that they fail to honor or kindly support the vulnerable orphan, and do not urge one another to feed the poor.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p338/r1.anchor: بل هناك شر من هذا القول وهو أن الله يكرمهم بالغنى فلا يؤدون ما يلزمهم فيه من اكرام اليتيم

QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r7.claim: They do not urge their families to feed a needy person who comes to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r7.anchor: أي لا يأمرون أهليهم بإطعام مسكين يجيئهم

QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r8.claim: They read tahadduna with open vowels as ‘you urge one another’; its form originally has two ta letters, one omitted, and Abu Ubayd prefers it.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r8.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون «ولا تحاضون» بفتح التاء والحاء والألف

QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r9.speaker: إبراهيم والشيزري عن الكسائي والسلمي
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r9.claim: They read tahaduna with a damma on the first ta, a mutual-urging form from the root meaning to incite.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:17-19/r9.anchor: وروي عن إبراهيم والشيزري عن الكسائي والسلمي «تحاضون» بضم التاء

QUTB-ZILAL:89:18/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:18/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:18/r1.claim: People fail to urge one another to feed even the needy who do not ask; mutual encouragement makes communal solidarity and directing others to good an Islamic norm.
QUTB-ZILAL:89:18/r1.anchor: وقد اعتبر عدم التحاض والتواصي على إطعام المسكين قبيحا مستنكرا

RAZI:89:18/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:18/r1.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:89:18/r1.claim: Muqātil glosses the phrase as failing to feed a poor person; its meaning is that they do not urge others to feed one.
RAZI:89:18/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل : ولا تطعمون مسكينا ، والمعنى لا تأمرون بإطعامه

RAZI:89:18/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:18/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:89:18/r2.claim: A reading with yāʾ, taḥāḍḍūn, means that people do not urge one another, with the first tāʾ of tatafāʿalūn elided.
RAZI:89:18/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ ولا تحاضون أراد تتحاضون فحذف تاء تتفاعلون

RAZI:89:18/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:18/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI:89:18/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s reading has the tāʾ vowelled with ḍamma and means mutual urging.
RAZI:89:18/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : { ولا تحاضون } بضم التاء من المحاضة

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.claim: Nay rebukes those who wrongly inferred divine favor or abasement from wealth; neglecting orphans and consuming their inheritance is one example of resulting injustice.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r1.anchor: Nay is a rebuke to those who make the errors implied in vv. 15–16

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.claim: These verses may be read in third-person plural instead of second-person plural; either reading is accepted.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r2.anchor: Some read all of these verses in the third-person plural rather than the second-person plural

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.claim: Failure to understand God's true honoring and abasing leads people to treat the less privileged inequitably.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r3.anchor: the implication of vv.17–20 is that failure to appreciate the true nature of God’s honoring and abasing leads people to act inequitably toward those who are less privileged

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r4.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r4.claim: The feeding exhortation has four readings: second-person transitive or reflexive, and third-person transitive or reflexive.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r4.anchor: It can be read in two ways in the second-person plural: transitive, taḥuḍḍūna

STUDYQURAN:89:17/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r5.claim: With a third-person reading, the criticism applies to the people described in verses 15–16.
STUDYQURAN:89:17/r5.anchor: When read in the third person, it is seen as applying to those mentioned in vv. 15–16

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads this and the next three verbs in third person, matching the generic singular human understood collectively.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو هذا والثلاثة بعده بياء الغيبة حملا على معنى الإنسان المتقدم

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.claim: The remaining readers use second-person forms, addressing generic humanity by a shift in person.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r2.anchor: والباقون بالتاء في الجميع خطابا للإنسان المراد به الجنس على طريق الالتفات

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r3.claim: The Kufans read taḥāḍḍūn, eliding one of the two original ta letters; it means that people urge one another.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r3.anchor: فحذف إحدى التاءين، أي: لا يحض بعضكم بعضا.

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r4.speaker: الكسائي، زيد بن علي، علقمة
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī is also reported, as are Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿAlqama, to read with a ḍamma on ta, meaning urge yourselves.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r4.anchor: بضم التاء، وهي قراءة زيد ابن علي وعلقمة، أي: تحاضون أنفسكم.

SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r5.claim: Other readers use taḥuḍḍūn, from urging someone; its object is omitted, either yourselves or others, or no object need be supplied.
SAMIN-DURR:89:17/r5.anchor: من حضه على كذا، أي: أغراه به. ومفعوله محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r1.claim: The phrase ʿalā ṭaʿām is governed by taḥāḍḍūn.
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r1.anchor: قوله: { على طعام }: متعلق بتحاضون. و

SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r2.claim: Ṭaʿām may retain its ordinary sense of food, stand for giving or supplying food with an omitted noun, or mean the verbal act of feeding without ellipsis.
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون على أصله من كونه اسما للمطعوم. ويكون على حذف مضاف، أي: على بذل

SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r3.claim: The tāʾ in al-turāth replaces wāw because the word derives from inheritance; tawalluj, tawrāh, and tukhmah are parallels.
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r3.anchor: بدل من الواو، لأنه من الوراثة. ومثله: تولج وتوراة وتخمة،

SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r4.claim: Lammā means collected together, as in al-Ḥuṭayʾa's example; al-jamm means abundant, with examples for water and hair and the crowd idiom.
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r4.anchor:
إذا كان لما يتبع الذم ربه
فلا قدس الرحمن تلك الطواحنا

SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r5.speaker: النابغة
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r5.claim: Al-Nābigha's line uses talummuhu for gathering or joining a companion in disarray, illustrating the root l-m-m.

SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:18/r6.claim: Zuhayr's poem uses jamm for abundant water; the text also mentions abundant hair and the idiom for a great crowd.

TAB:89:18/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:18/r1.claim: Qatāda says God rejects the idea that wealth makes a person honored or poverty makes one disgraced; honor comes through obedience and disgrace through disobedience.
TAB:89:18/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  وأمّا إذَا ما ابْتَلاهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُ فَيقُولُ رَبّي أهانني

TAB:89:18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB:89:18/r2.claim: Another interpretation says the person should praise God in both prosperity and poverty rather than thank Him for wealth but complain about want.
TAB:89:18/r2.anchor: وقالوا :  معنى الكلام :  كلاّ ،   أي لم يكن ينبغي أن يكون هكذا ،   ولكن كان ينبغي أن يحمده

TAB:89:18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r3.speaker: author
TAB:89:18/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Qatāda's view because the following verses identify the conduct behind disgrace: failing to honor orphans and urge feeding the poor.
TAB:89:18/r3.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب :  القول الذي ذكرناه عن قتادة ،   لدلالة قوله بَلْ لا تُكْرِمُونَ الْيَتِيمَ

TAB:89:18/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r4.speaker: author
TAB:89:18/r4.claim: The address says that people were disgraced for not honoring the orphan; the failure to urge feeding the poor explains the same neglect.
TAB:89:18/r4.anchor: بل إنما أهنت من أَهَنت من أجل أنه لا يكرم اليتيم ،   فأخرج الكلام على الخطاب ،   فقال

TAB:89:18/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r5.speaker: قراء المدينة وأهل الكوفة
TAB:89:18/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and the general Kufan readers use a second-person form with alif, meaning people do not encourage one another to feed the poor.
TAB:89:18/r5.anchor: أبو جعفر وعامة قرّاء الكوفة بَلْ لا تُكْرِمونَ الْيَتِيمَ وَلا تَحَاضّونَ بالتاء أيضا وفتحها ،   وإثبات الألف

TAB:89:18/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r6.speaker: بعض قراء مكة وعامة قراء المدينة
TAB:89:18/r6.claim: Some Meccan and most Medinan readers omit the alif in the second-person form, meaning people do not urge feeding the poor.
TAB:89:18/r6.anchor: بعض قرّاء مكة وعامة قرّاء المدينة ،   بالتاء وفتحها وحذف الألف :  «وَلا تَحُضّونَ » بمعنى

TAB:89:18/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r7.speaker: عامة قراء البصرة
TAB:89:18/r7.claim: The Basran readers use the third person without alif and read the surrounding verbs in third person as a report about those people.
TAB:89:18/r7.anchor: عامة قرّاء البصرة :  «يَحُضّونَ » بالياء وحذف الألف ،   بمعنى :  ولا يكرم القائلون

TAB:89:18/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:89:18/r8.claim: Another reported reading uses a second-person form with ḍamma and alif, explained as failing to look after one another.
TAB:89:18/r8.anchor: وقد ذُكر عن بعضهم أنه قرأ :  «تُحاضّونَ » بالتاء وضمها وإثبات الألف ،   بمعنى :  ولا تحافظون .

TAB:89:18/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:18/r9.speaker: author
TAB:89:18/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī accepts the three principal regional readings as sound in meaning, so whichever a reader uses is correct.
TAB:89:18/r9.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي :  أن هذه قراءات معروفات في قراءة الأمصار ،   أعني القراءات الثلاث صحيحات المعاني

TAB-FULL:v24p378/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r1.speaker: عامة قراء الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r1.claim: Most Kufan readers use the direct-address tāʾ form with an alif, meaning people do not urge one another to feed the poor.
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r1.anchor: وعامة قراء الكوفة {بل لا تكرمون اليتيم ولا تحاضون} [الفجر: 18] بالتاء أيضا وفتحها، وإثبات الألف فيها

TAB-FULL:v24p378/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r2.speaker: بعض قراء مكة وعامة قراء المدينة
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r2.claim: Some Meccan and most Medinan readers omit the alif: people do not urge feeding the poor.
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r2.anchor: قرأ ذلك بعض قراء مكة وعامة قراء المدينة، بالتاء وفتحها وحذف الألف

TAB-FULL:v24p378/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r3.speaker: أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r3.claim: The Basran readers use third-person yāʾ forms for this verb and the accompanying words.
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r3.anchor: وكذلك يقرأ الذين ذكرنا من أهل البصرة (يكرمون) وسائر الحروف معها بالياء

TAB-FULL:v24p378/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r4.claim: Another reported reading adds an alif and uses a doubled ḥāʾ, meaning they do not maintain or look after the poor.
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر عن بعضهم أنه قرأ: (تحاضون) بالتاء وضمها وإثبات الألف، بمعنى: ولا تحافظون

TAB-FULL:v24p378/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī regards the three principal regional readings as sound in meaning and accepts any of them.
TAB-FULL:v24p378/r5.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي: أن هذه قراءات معروفات في قراءة الأمصار، أعني القراءات الثلاث صحيحات المعاني

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r7.claim: The rebuke denies that wealth equals honor and poverty equals humiliation: withholding or granting is a test, and their failure to honor orphans and encourage feeding the poor disproves their claim to dignity.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r7.anchor: ردع لقولهم إن الكرامة هي في الغنى والتنعم، وفي الفقر والفقدان هوان ومذلة

TABATABAI:89:15-18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r8.claim: The shift from third person to direct address, along with the contrastive “rather,” intensifies the reproach.
TABATABAI:89:15-18/r8.anchor: وفي الإضراب مضافا إلى أصل الردع تقريع ولتشديد هذا التقريع وقع الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

TABATABAI:89:17-22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r2.claim: The wording comes from “you do not urge one another” and means they do not encourage one another to give to the destitute, because they love wealth.
TABATABAI:89:17-22/r2.anchor: أصله ولا تتحاضون، وهو تحريض بعضهم بعضا على التصدق على المساكين المعدمين

ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r5.claim: One reading has lā taḥāḍḍūn; another has lā taḥāḍḍūna concerning urging food for the poor.
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r5.anchor:
(ولا تحضون)
ويقرأ (ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين).

ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r6.claim: They used to consume orphans' property greedily and hastily; the reprimand then says they fail to honor orphans and urge feeding the poor.
ZAJJAJ:v5p322/r6.anchor: وكانوا يأكلون أموال اليتامى إسرافا وبدارا فقال

TABRISI:89:25/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:25/r4.speaker: أهل الكوفة، أبو جعفر
TABRISI:89:25/r4.claim: The Kufans and Abū Jaʿfar read lā taḥāḍḍūn as mutual urging.
TABRISI:89:25/r4.anchor: وقرأ لا تحاضون أهل الكوفة وأبو جعفر

TABRISI:89:25/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:25/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:25/r19.claim: Lā taḥuḍḍūn means you do not urge or encourage feeding the poor; lā taḥāḍḍūn means you do not urge one another.
TABRISI:89:25/r19.anchor: ومعنى لا تحضون على طعام المسكين لا تأمرون به ولا تبعثون عليه

ASAD-NOTES:89:17#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:89:17#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:89:17#n11/r1.claim: The phrase means people feel no urge to feed the needy, paralleling 107:3.
ASAD-NOTES:89:17#n11/r1.anchor: I.e., "you feel no urge to feed the needy"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512#2/r1.claim: They do not feed the poor or encourage others to do so, as in the parallel rebuke at 69:34.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512#2/r1.anchor:
قال مقاتل: ولا يطعمون مسكينا (¬3).
والمعنى: لا يأمرون بإطعامه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512#2/r2.claim: The reading “yuhaddun” means that people do not urge one another, with the initial ta of the reciprocal form elided.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p512#2/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ: "يحاضون" أراد تتحاضون، فحذف تاء تتفاعلون،

WAHIDI-QT:89:18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:18/r1.claim: They neither urge others to feed the poor nor help do so themselves.
WAHIDI-QT:89:18/r1.anchor: { ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين } لا تأمرون به ولا تعينون عليه

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.claim: The whole rebuke also has readings in the third-person plural rather than the second-person plural.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zum gesamten Scheltwort V. 17–20 existieren auch Lesungen in der 3. statt 2. Person Plural

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r1.claim: The triad of feeding, orphans, and the poor appears elsewhere in early and middle Meccan passages, including 107:2–3 and 90:11–16.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die drei Elemente Speisung – Waise – Armer tauchen in früh- und mittelmekkanischer Zeit u. a. in 107:2.3 und 90:11–16 auf

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r2.claim: The consonantal text of taḥāḍḍūna could instead be read yaḥuḍḍūna, by analogy with 107:3.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-18:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Das Konsonantengerüst von taḥāḍḍūna ließe sich auch analog zu 107:3

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.claim: Verses 17–20 specify the earlier charges against ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh: neglecting help for poor people and orphans, metonymically the vulnerable, and excessive love of possessions.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r1.anchor: Wie in anderen frühmekkanischen Texten werden insbesondere die Unterlassung von Hilfeleistungen gegenüber Armen und Waisen

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.claim: These motifs also occur in biblical prophetic books and likely belonged to a literary genre familiar to the hearers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:17-20:kommentar/r2.anchor: Es handelt sich dabei um Motive, die auch in den biblischen Prophetenbüchern präsent sind und wohl auch als Elemente eines den Hörern vertrauten literarischen Genres fungiert haben dürften.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.claim: Passing life’s test requires gratitude for God’s unearned gifts and patience when they are withheld, plus sharing with the poor and vulnerable and encouraging organized social solidarity; Meccan ethics summarize this as reverence for God’s command and compassion for His creatures.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r5.anchor: bu hususta toplumsal bir duyarlılığın gelişmesine, dayanışma ve yardımlaşmanın kurumsal bir hale gelmesine katkıda bulunmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.claim: The passage sharply criticizes polytheist arrogance, selfish indifference to others, and mad attachment to wealth while teaching Muslims the religious and moral basis for life under God’s will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:15/r6.anchor: müşrik Araplar’daki Allah’a karşı küstahlık derecesine kadar varan benlik iddiası, “öteki”ne karşı tam bir sorumsuzluk ve ilgisizliğe götüren egoizm ve çılgınca bir mal tutkusu

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r5.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r5.claim: These readers pronounce تحضون with تاء and without alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر: تحضون [الفجر/ 18] بالتاء بغير ألف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads تحضون with ياء and without alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده بالياء بغير ألف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r7.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r7.claim: These readers use تاء plus alif in تحاضون.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r7.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي: تحاضون بالتاء والألف،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r8.claim: The verb means that people neither command nor encourage others to feed the poor, as the parallel wording in al-Ḥāqqa confirms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي: كأن معنى لا تحضون على طعام المسكين: لا تأمرون به ولا تبعثون عليه،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r9.claim: تحاضون is treated as a shortened form of تتفاعلون; reciprocal exhortation does not fit because these people do not spur one another on, so its sense is تحضون.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r9.anchor: ومن قرأ: تحاضون على تتفاعلون، من هذا، فحذف تاء تتفاعلون،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r10.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r10.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r10.claim: The poetic example تحاسنت means حسنته, supporting a derived form with the simple transitive sense rather than reciprocal action.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r10.anchor:
تحاسنت به الوشي قرات الرياح وخورها
أي: حسنته،

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r11.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r11.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r11.claim: Other examples likewise use an augmented form with a simple sense: استقر means قر, and استعلاه means علاه; the Qur'anic phrase means He is above it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p409/r11.anchor: استقر في مكانه بمعنى: قر، وليس المعنى على أنه استدعى القرار،

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.claim: The verbs addressing the audience and their conduct vary between yāʾ and tāʾ; Kūfan readers alone add an alif in تحاضون. The cited rationale for yāʾ is continuation from the preceding context.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p370/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم ﴾ ﴿ ولا تحاضون ﴾ و ﴿ يأكلون ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:89:18:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:18:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:18:3#1/r1.claim: Form I taḥuḍḍūna means you urge, reducing the explicit mutual force of Form VI while keeping direct address.
QIRAAT-ER:89:18:3#1/r1.anchor: Canonical reading shifts to Form I 2MP

QIRAAT-ER:89:18:3#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:18:3#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:18:3#2/r1.claim: Form I yaḥuḍḍūna means they urge and changes direct address to third-person report.
QIRAAT-ER:89:18:3#2/r1.anchor: Canonical reading shifts to Form I 3MP

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r1.claim: The phrase “for food” can mean “for feeding,” though Abū Ḥayyān prefers supplying an omitted “giving of,” yielding “giving food.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p475/r1.anchor: على طعام، يجوز أن يكون بمعنى إطعام، كالعطاء بمعنى الإعطاء، والأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r1.claim: The form “taḥāḍḍūn” drops one of the two tāʾs; people fail to urge and encourage one another to feed the needy.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r1.anchor: ولا تحاضون بحذف إحدى التاءين من تتحاضون أي ولا يحض ويحث بعضكم بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r2.claim: “Food of the needy” means feeding them, with ṭaʿām used as a verbal noun like ʿaṭāʾ for giving.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r2.anchor: على طعام المسكين أي على إطعامه فالطعام مصدر بمعنى الإطعام كالعطاء بمعنى الإعطاء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers taking the word as actual food and supplying an omitted “giving”: urging one another to provide the needy's food.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r3.anchor: وزعم أبو حيان أن الأولى أن يراد به الشيء المطعوم ويكون الكلام على حذف مضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r4.claim: The needy here includes the poor generally; readings vary in the vowel of the tāʾ and between second- and third-person forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r4.anchor: والمراد بالمسكين ما يعم الفقير وقرأ عبد الله وعلقمة وزيد بن علي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r5.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r5.claim: Abd Allah, ʿAlqama, Zayd ibn ʿAli, Ibn al-Mubarak, and al-Shirizi from al-Kisaʾi read with a ḍamma on the tāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r5.anchor: قرأ عبد الله وعلقمة وزيد بن علي وعبد الله بن المبارك والشيرزي عن الكسائي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r6.claim: Abu ʿAmr, al-Hasan, and others read the verb in the third person without an alif after ḥāʾ; the other seven read it in second-person address.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ومن سمعت الحسن ومن معه ولا يحضون بياء الغيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r7.claim: The verb may take an omitted object such as oneself, one's family, or anyone; al-Alusi prefers an intransitive reading that generalizes the rebuke.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p127/r7.anchor: وجوز وهو الأولى أن يكون منزلا منزلة اللازم للتعميم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r4.claim: They do not urge others to feed the poor.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r5.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Kufan readers vocalize taḥāḍḍūna with an open ḥāʾ and a following alif, meaning people do not urge one another to feed the poor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p421#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة: "تحاضون" بفتح الحاء وألف بعدها، أي لا يحض بعضكم بعضا عليه

BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.claim: These verses connect tyranny and corruption with greed-driven individualism: dishonoring orphans, failing to urge care for the needy, plundering inheritance, and loving wealth until conscience, insight, and the heart are dulled.
BINTSHATI:v2p153/r6.anchor: وبهذا البيان المحكم، ترتبط الآيات التي لفتت ذا حجر إلى مصير الذين طغوا في البلاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r6.claim: Urging one's household and others to feed the needy is greater than giving alone because exhortation entails giving, while giving need not prompt others.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r6.anchor: الإحسان بالحث على الإعطاء أعظم من الإعطاء لأنه يلزم منه الإعطاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r7.claim: The needy person is treated as a partner in the wealthy person's property to the extent of zakat.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r7.anchor: فكانت إضافته إليه إشارة إلى أنه شريك للغني ما له بقدر الزكاة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r8.claim: The wording first speaks of the human in the singular to generalize, then uses plural verbs to address the human species collectively.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p419/r8.anchor: وأفرد أولا لأنه أنص على التعميم وجمع ثانيا إعلاما بأن المراد الجنس

DURR-FULL:v8p508/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet recited the following verbs with yāʾ in the reading about honoring the orphan and urging the feeding of the poor.
DURR-FULL:v8p508/r7.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ / بل لا يكرمون اليتيم ولا يحضون / بالياء

TAB:89:17/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر وعامة قراء الكوفة
TAB:89:17/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and most Kufan readers use second-person forms and taḥāḍḍūn with an alif, meaning you do not urge one another to feed the poor.
TAB:89:17/r7.anchor: فقرأه من أهل المدينة أبو جعفر وعامة قرّاء الكوفة بَلْ لا تُكْرِمونَ الْيَتيمَ وَلا تَحاضّونَ بالتاء أيضا وفتحها ، وإثبات الألف فيها

TAB:89:17/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r8.speaker: بعض قراء مكة وعامة قراء المدينة
TAB:89:17/r8.claim: Some Meccan and most Medinan readers use second-person taḥuḍḍūn without an alif, meaning you do not urge feeding the poor.
TAB:89:17/r8.anchor: قرأ ذلك بعض قرّاء مكة وعامة قرّاء المدينة ، بالتاء وفتحها وحذف الألف

TAB:89:17/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r9.speaker: عامة قراء البصرة
TAB:89:17/r9.claim: Basran readers use third-person ya forms and no alif, reporting that those people do not honor the orphan or urge feeding the poor.

TAB:89:17/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r10.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:89:17/r10.claim: A further reported reading has taḥāḍḍūn with a damma on the ta, meaning that you do not mutually preserve or encourage one another.
TAB:89:17/r10.anchor: وقد ذُكر عن بعضهم أنه قرأ

TAB:89:17/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:17/r11.speaker: author
TAB:89:17/r11.claim: Al-Tabari regards the three established regional readings as sound in meaning, so a reciter is correct with any of them.
TAB:89:17/r11.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي : أن هذه قراءات معروفات في قراءة الأمصار ، أعني القراءات الثلاث صحيحات المعاني ، فبأي ذلك قرأ القارىء فمصيب

NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.claim: The Basrans except al-Zubayrī from Rawḥ read the four verbs in third person; the others, including al-Zubayrī, address the audience directly.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r9.anchor: فقرأ البصريان سوى الزبيري عن روح بالغيب في الأربعة، وقرأ الباقون بالخطاب ومعهم الزبيري عن روح

NASHR:v2p399#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r10.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and the Kufans add an alif after the ḥāʾ in تحاضون and lengthen it before the following sukūn.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r10.anchor: وأثبت الألف بعد الحاء في تحاضون أبو جعفر، والكوفيون، ويمدون للساكن

ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r1.claim: The continuation of al-Zamakhsharī’s quotation discusses urging people to feed the poor and describes consuming and coveting food like cattle.
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r1.anchor: وحض أهله على طعام المسكين ويأكلونه أكل الأنعام ويحبونه فيشحون به ، انتهى .

ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r2.speaker: الحديث
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r2.claim: A hadith says the most beloved home to God is one in which an orphan is treated honorably; no grading is stated.
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث : « أحب البيوت إلى الله تعالى بيت فيه يتيم مكرم »

ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري وأبو عمر
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r3.claim: These readers use third-person forms for “honor,” “urge,” “eat,” and “love,” while the remaining Seven use second-person address.
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء وقتادة والجحدري وأبو عمر : يكرمون ولا يحضون ، ويأكلون ويحبون بياء الغيبة فيها ؛ وباقي السبعة ، بتاء الخطاب

ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة والكوفيون وابن مقسم والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r4.claim: These readers use taḥāḍḍūn with fatḥa and an alif, from tataḥāḍḍūn, meaning that people urge one another.
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r4.anchor: وأبو جعفر وشيبة والكوفيون وابن مقسم : تحاضون بفتح التاء والألف أصله تتحاضون ، وهي قراءة الأعمش ، أي يحض بعضكم بعضاً

ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r5.speaker: عبد الله أو علقمة وزيد بن علي وعبد الله بن المبارك والشيرزي عن الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r5.claim: This group has the same reciprocal sense but reads the tāʾ with ḍamma, meaning that people exhort one another.
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r5.anchor: وعبد الله أو علقمة وزيد بن عليّ وعبد الله بن المبارك والشيرزي عن الكسائي : كذلك

ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r6.claim: The reciprocal forms tafāʿala and fāʿala can also carry the meaning of the simple faʿala form.
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r6.anchor: وتفاعل وفاعل يأتي بمعنى فعل أيضاً .

ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r7.claim: ʿAlā ṭaʿām may mean feeding, like al-ʿaṭāʾ for al-iʿṭāʾ; better is to supply an omitted noun, “the giving of food.”
ABUHAYYAN:89:18/r7.anchor: { على طعام } ، يجوز أن يكون بمعنى إطعام ، كالعطاء بمعنى الإعطاء ، والأولى أن يكون على حذف مضاف ، أي على بذل طعام .

ALUSI:89:18/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:18/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:18/r1.claim: Taḥāḍḍūn drops one of the two tāʾs in tataḥāḍḍūn and means people do not urge one another.
ALUSI:89:18/r1.anchor: بحذف احدى التاءين من تتحاضون أي ولا يحض ويحث بعضكم بعضا

ALUSI:89:18/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:18/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:18/r2.claim: The phrase means urging one another to feed the poor; ṭaʿām is a verbal noun meaning feeding, like ʿaṭāʾ for giving.
ALUSI:89:18/r2.anchor: أي على إطعامه فالطعام مصدر بمعنى الإطعام كالعطاء بمعنى الإعطاء

ALUSI:89:18/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:18/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:89:18/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers taking ṭaʿām as the food itself, with an omitted word meaning providing the poor person's food.
ALUSI:89:18/r3.anchor: وزعم أبو حيان أن الأولى أن يراد به الشيء المطعوم ويكون الكلام على حذف مضاف

ALUSI:89:18/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:18/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:18/r4.claim: Al-miskīn here broadly includes both the needy and the poor.

ALUSI:89:18/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:18/r5.speaker: عبد الله وعلقمة وزيد بن علي وعبد الله بن المبارك والشيرزي عن الكسائي
ALUSI:89:18/r5.claim: These readers use the community reading's form but with ḍamma on the tāʾ, tuḥāḍḍūn, from mutual exhortation.
ALUSI:89:18/r5.anchor: قرأ عبد الله وعلقمة وزيد بن علي وعبد الله بن المبارك والشيرزي عن الكسائي كقراءة الجماعة إلا أنهم ضموا تاء تحاضون

ALUSI:89:18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:18/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو والحسن ومن معه
ALUSI:89:18/r6.claim: Abū ʿAmr, al-Ḥasan and associated readers use third-person lā yaḥuḍḍūna without an alif after ḥāʾ; the other seven use second-person lā taḥuḍḍūna, and the same person shift applies to the next two verbs.
ALUSI:89:18/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ومن سمعت الحسن ومن معه ولا يحضون بياء الغيبة ولا ألف بعد الحاء

ALUSI:89:18/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:18/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:18/r7.claim: With either reading, yaḥuḍḍūna can be transitive with an omitted object—oneself, one's family, or anyone—or intransitive; the intransitive reading is preferable for its generality.
ALUSI:89:18/r7.anchor: والفعل على القراءتين جوز أن يكون متعديا ومفعوله محذوف فقيل أنفسهم أو أنفسكم

BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.speaker: أهل البصرة
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.claim: Basra reads the four verbs about honoring, urging, eating, and loving in the third person with yāʾ; the other readers use second-person tāʾ.
BAGHAWI:89:17/r6.anchor: قرأ أهل لبصرة :  "  يكرمون ،   ويحضون ،   ويأكلون ،   ويحبون "  بالياء فيهن ،   وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء

BAGHAWI:89:18/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:18/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:18/r1.claim: They do not urge others to feed the poor.

BAGHAWI:89:18/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:18/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة
BAGHAWI:89:18/r2.claim: Abu Jafar and the Kufans read the verb with an open ḥāʾ and a following alif, meaning that people do not urge one another.
BAGHAWI:89:18/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأهل الكوفة : { تحاضون } بفتح الحاء وألف بعدها ،   أي لا يحض بعضكم بعضاً عليه

BAYDAWI:89:18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:18/r1.claim: Their conduct is worse evidence of greed than their claims: they neither support orphans with care and spending nor urge even their own families to feed the poor.
BAYDAWI:89:18/r1.anchor: بل فعلهم أسوأ من قولهم وأدل على تهالكهم بالمال

BAYDAWI:89:18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:18/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
BAYDAWI:89:18/r2.claim: The Kūfan readers use the form taḥāḍḍūn.

BIQAI:89:18/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:18/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:18/r1.claim: Love of wealth stops people urging generosity: they may hoard when the recipient is wealthier, or fear reciprocal demands from an equal and urge help for someone else instead.
BIQAI:89:18/r1.anchor: لا يمنعه من حث غيره على الخير إلا حب الدنيا

BIQAI:89:18/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:18/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:18/r2.claim: Urging another person to give is greater than giving oneself, because encouragement necessarily entails giving whereas giving alone does not entail encouragement.
BIQAI:89:18/r2.anchor: الإحسان بالحث على الإعطاء أعظم من الإعطاء لأنه يلزم منه الإعطاء

BIQAI:89:18/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:18/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:18/r3.claim: The rebuke concerns failing to strongly urge one's family and others to give food generously to the poor; calling it their food implies the poor share in the wealthy person's property to the extent of zakat.
BIQAI:89:18/r3.anchor: يحثون حثاً عظيماً لأهلهم ولا لغيرهم

DURR:89:15/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:15/r3.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:15/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf reports that the Prophet recited the following clauses with yāʾ (third-person plural); al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:89:15/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ { بل لا يكرمون اليتيم

DURR:89:16/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:16/r3.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:16/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf reports that the Prophet recited the following clauses with yāʾ (third-person plural); al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR:89:16/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ { بل لا يكرمون اليتيم

DURR:89:20/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r13.speaker: عاصم
DURR:89:20/r13.claim: Asim reads the clauses with second-person tāʾ in tukrimūn, taḥāḍḍūn (lengthened and unhamzated), and taʾ in turath, with lamman geminated.
DURR:89:20/r13.anchor: عن عاصم رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ { كلا بل لا تكرمون اليتيم } بالتاء ورفع التاء { ولا تحاضون } ممدودة

DURR:89:20/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r14.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:20/r14.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Prophet read all four clauses with yāʾ, in the third-person plural.
DURR:89:20/r14.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ { كلا بل لا يكرمون اليتيم

DURR:89:20/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:20/r15.speaker: النبي
DURR:89:20/r15.claim: Ibn Umar likewise reports the Prophet reading the clauses through 'they love wealth' with yāʾ throughout.
DURR:89:20/r15.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنه قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ

IBNASHUR:89:18/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:18/r1.claim: Failing even to urge others to feed implies a fortiori that they themselves do not feed: they will not mediate, much less give.

IBNASHUR:89:18/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:18/r2.claim: Ṭaʿām may mean food itself, yielding an exhortation to give the poor person food, with the annexation marking entitlement.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r2.anchor: { طعام } يجوز أن يكون اسما بمعنى المطعوم

IBNASHUR:89:18/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:18/r3.claim: Alternatively, ṭaʿām is the verbal noun of feeding, with the poor person as object: the rich are not urged to feed the poor.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون اسم مصدر أطعم

IBNASHUR:89:18/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:18/r4.claim: Miskīn means a poor person; its explanation was given earlier in Sūrat al-Tawba.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r4.anchor: و { المسكين } : الفقير وتقدم في سورة براءة

IBNASHUR:89:18/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:18/r5.claim: Reciprocal implication supplies omitted complements: not honoring orphans entails not urging their guardians to honor them; not urging food entails not feeding the poor from one’s wealth.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r5.anchor: وقد حصل في الآية احتباك لأنهم لما نفي إكرامهم اليتيم وقوبل بنفي أن يحضوا على طعام المسكين

IBNASHUR:89:18/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:18/r6.claim: Urging others to feed can stand for feeding oneself, because someone who urges an act wants to do it and performs it when able.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الحض على الطعام كناية عن الإطعام لأن من يحض على فعل شيء يكون راغبا

IBNASHUR:89:18/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:18/r7.claim: The call to urge truth and patience likewise means practicing them as well as encouraging them.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r7.anchor: أي عملوا بالحق وصبروا وتواصوا بهما

IBNASHUR:89:18/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r8.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:89:18/r8.claim: Most readers use second-person forms, shifting from the earlier third-person framing to confront the audience with a more forceful rebuke.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : « لا تكرمون ، ولا تحضون ، وتأكلون ، وتحبون » بالمثناة الفوقية على الخطاب

IBNASHUR:89:18/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
IBNASHUR:89:18/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Yaʿqūb read the verbs in third person, informing the Prophet and believers of the audience’s conduct, as in the cited passage.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r9.anchor: وقرأها أبو عمرو ويعقوب بالمثناة التحتية على الغيبة لتعريف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم والمسلمين بذلك

IBNASHUR:89:18/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r10.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:89:18/r10.claim: Most readers vocalize taḥuḍḍūna with a ḍamma on the ḥāʾ as the imperfect of ḥaḍḍa.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { ولا تحضُّون } بضم الحاء مضارع حضّ

IBNASHUR:89:18/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:18/r11.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف
IBNASHUR:89:18/r11.claim: These readers use taḥāḍḍūna with fatḥa and an alif, reduced from tataḥāḍḍūna, meaning that people urge one another not to feed.
IBNASHUR:89:18/r11.anchor: وقرأه عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وخلف { تَحَاضُّون } بفتح الحاء وألف بعدها

IBNATIYYA:89:18/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read yaḥuḍḍūn, meaning that people urge one another or urge themselves.
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر «يحضون » بمعنى : يحض بعضهم بعضاً أو تحضون أنفسكم ،

IBNATIYYA:89:18/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r2.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r2.claim: Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read taḥāḍḍūn with fatḥa on the tāʾ, meaning that groups urge one another.
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي «تحاضون » بفتح التاء بعنى تتحاضون ، أي يحض قوم قوماً ،

IBNATIYYA:89:18/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r3.claim: Abu Amr reads yaḥuḍḍūn with a prefixed yāʾ and no alif.
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو و «يحضون » بياء من تحت مفتوحة وبغير ألف

IBNATIYYA:89:18/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak reads tuḥāḍḍūn with ḍamma on the tāʾ, on the pattern of tuqātilūn, meaning to urge yourselves or one another; al-Shirazi also transmits it from al-Kisa'i.
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r4.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن المبار : «تُحاضون » بضم التاء على وزن تقاتلون ، أي أنفسكم أي بعضكم بعضاً ورواها الشيرزي عن الكسائي

IBNATIYYA:89:18/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r5.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r5.claim: Abu Ali says the fāʿala pattern can mean faʿala, citing taḥāsana and takhāzara as examples; the poet is not named in the passage.
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r5.anchor: وقد يجيء فاعلت بمعنى فعلت وهذا منه ، وإلى هذا ذهب أبو علي وأنشد : تحاسنت به الوشى

IBNATIYYA:89:18/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r6.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r6.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads tataḥāḍḍūn with two tāʾs.

IBNATIYYA:89:18/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r7.claim: Ṭaʿām here can mean feeding the poor rather than the food itself.

IBNATIYYA:89:18/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r8.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r8.claim: Others take the phrase as the actual food one eats and understand an omitted construction in the wording.
IBNATIYYA:89:18/r8.anchor: وقال قوم أراد نفس طعامه الذي يأكل ، ففي الكلام حذف تقديره على بدل { طعام المسكين }

IBNKATHIR:89:18/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:18/r1.claim: They do not urge one another to be kind to the poor and needy or encourage each other to feed them.
IBNKATHIR:89:18/r1.anchor: يعني : لا يأمرون بالإحسان إلى الفقراء والمساكين ، ويحث بعضهم على بعض في ذلك

KASHSHAF:89:17/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:17/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:17/r3.claim: They do not urge their households to feed the poor, and consume wealth like cattle.
KASHSHAF:89:17/r3.anchor: وحض أهله على طعام المسكين ويأكلونه أكل الأنعام

KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:17/r5.claim: The verbs here and what follows are read in either third person, “they,” or second person, “you.”

KASHSHAF:89:18/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:18/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:18/r1.claim: Taḥāḍḍūn means that you urge one another; Ibn Masʿūd's reading has the tāʾ vowelled with ḍamma, from muḥāḍḍa.

NASAFI:89:17/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:17/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:17/r2.claim: They also fail to urge their own households to feed the poor.
NASAFI:89:17/r2.anchor: إكرام اليتيم بالمبرة وحض أهله على طعام المسكين

NASAFI:89:18/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:18/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:18/r2.claim: They also fail to urge their own households to feed the poor.
NASAFI:89:18/r2.anchor: إكرام اليتيم بالمبرة وحض أهله على طعام المسكين

NASAFI:89:20/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:20/r4.speaker: البصري
NASAFI:89:20/r4.claim: The Basran reading uses third-person forms yukrimun, yahuddun, ya’kulun, and yuhibbun for the corresponding second-person forms in verses 17–20.
NASAFI:89:20/r4.anchor: { يكرمون } { وَلاَ يحضون } { وَيَأْكُلُونَ } { وَّيُحِبُّونَ } بصري

QURTUBI:89:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:18/r1.claim: They do not instruct their families to feed a needy person who comes to them.
QURTUBI:89:18/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " ولا تحاضون على طعام المسكين " أي لا يأمرون أهليهم بإطعام مسكين يجيئهم

QURTUBI:89:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:18/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI:89:18/r2.claim: The Kufans read with fatḥa on tāʾ, ḥāʾ, and alif, meaning people urge one another; it derives from تتحاضون with one tāʾ elided. Abu Ubayd prefers it.
QURTUBI:89:18/r2.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون " ولا تحاضون " بفتح التاء والحاء والألف . أي يحض بعضهم بعضا . وأصله تتحاضون ، فحذف إحدى التاءين لدلالة الكلام عليها . وهو اختيار أبي عبيد

QURTUBI:89:18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:18/r3.speaker: إبراهيم والشيزري عن الكسائي والسلمي
QURTUBI:89:18/r3.claim: Ibrahim, al-Shizari from al-Kisai, and al-Sulami are reported to read with ḍamma on tāʾ; it is the reciprocal form of urging.
QURTUBI:89:18/r3.anchor: وروي عن إبراهيم والشيزري عن الكسائي والسلمي " تحاضون " بضم التاء ، وهو تفاعلون من الحض ، وهو الحث
